title: Learning Lab Agreement — Eligibility and Participation
content: A person deploying AI in Utah may enter either a Regulatory Mitigation Agreement (RMA) — which waives specified law in exchange for safeguards, data sharing, and disclosures — or a Joint Interpretation Agreement (JIA) — which clarifies how existing statute applies to a specific AI use without waiver. Agreements run for an initial twelve months with up to two twelve-month extensions, counterparties include OAIP plus the relevant state agency (or the judiciary, a state-funded higher or public education institution, or a political subdivision under HB 320), and participants must satisfy five statutory eligibility prongs.
pub:source_review_unresolved: enacted (2026-03-19) and the Introduced month (2026-01) are not in the enrolled copy; the le.utah.gov HB0320 static page renders no status table. Rows are marked unconfirmed and the enacted field is unchanged.
Whether OAIP filed annual reports in 2024 or 2025 (and so the ordinal of the 2026 report) is unverified; the row is relabeled without an ordinal.

The PubLedge closing paragraph still characterizes the JIA as the "interpretation" instrument; the statute's own term is "clarifies the application of a provision of state law or rule". Whether JIAs support reliance is left to a human editor.

The commerce.utah.gov/ai/learning-lab/ link (404 on 2026-09-24 per ops/evidence/utah-overdue-dispositions-2026-09-23.json url_checks) was replaced with the retrieved OAIP home page; a dedicated current Learning Lab page needs human confirmation.
amends (us-ut-legislature-statute-2024-sb149) is unchanged; HB 320 amends and renumbers sections SB 149 enacted, so the source does not contradict it.

Prongs (a), (d) and (e) in What Counts remain paraphrases and were not re-worded; "limited to the statute, use case, and deployment period" is not statutory wording for prong (e) (scale, scope, and duration of testing limited based on risk assessments).
